thread:
Anya K: Heads-up: nightly perf run showed a ~12% p99 token-latency regression for the continuous batcher when KV hit-rate exceeded ~78%. Repro logs attached.
Samir: ugh. Is this only when KV hit-rate is high? Could be batching forming too-large micro-batches and picking the wrong kernel path.
Lee: I think it's an interaction: when many requests are KV-hits the sequence lengths are shorter but we still target the larger token budget, so batches mix short + long sequences -> kernel selection oscillates.
Marta: do we have a profile? flamegraph /nvprof traces?
Anya K: Added a short profile snippet from nightly canary (perf-bot):
```
# top of kernel timeline
conv_attention_kernel.cu        48.2ms
kv_cache_merge.cu              12.4ms
matmul_big_opt.cu              30.1ms  # selected for mixed shapes
small_te_matmul.cu             6.3ms
```
Looks like matmul_big_opt gets selected more often despite many short sequences.
Noah: That matches the batch formation heuristic: token_budget_default=1024; large budget encourages filling bigger batches even when many short requests present.
Samir: Proposal: 1) make token_budget adaptive to recent seq-length distribution (e.g. target = min(1024, 1.1 * P90_tokens)) 2) prefer homogenous batches by seq-length bucketing for ~50ms window 3) tag requests with `kernel_hint:"small"` when seq < 64 to bias kernel selection.
Lee: +1 on adaptive token budget. Also add soft backpressure: when queue depth > X and KV-hit-rate > 60% reduce token_budget by 25% and emit a soft-429 to clients with Retry-After header to give runtime breathing room.
Marta: We should avoid hard 429 floods. Soft-429 = respond with 429 + x-retry-suggestion but still accept a small proportion for canary monitoring.
Anya K: Draft patch for admission config (prototype):
```
admission:
  token_budget_base: 1024
  adaptive:
    enabled: true
    scale_factor: 1.1
    percentile: 90
  kv_aware:
    enabled: true
    hit_threshold_pct: 60
    reduce_pct_on_pressure: 25
  homogenous_buckets_ms: 50
  kernel_tagging:
    enabled: true
    small_seq_threshold: 64
```
Noah: Quick experiment results from local sim: adaptive token_budget reduced p99 by ~9% and decreased kernel oscillation events by 70% (measured as kernel-change-per-batch).
perf-bot: Canary deploy queued to canary-3 with flag `batching-adaptive-tokenbudget-v1`.
deploy-bot: canary-3 deploy started at 1933456895 :rocket:
Samir: If canary looks good, plan to default kv-aware and homogenous bucketing but keep kernel_tagging off until we validate no model-quality regressions.
Marta: Add a short-term telemetry spike: emit `batch.kernel_switches` metric and `admission.token_budget_effective` per route. Want to see per-model breakdown.
Anya K: Action items:
- Samir & Lee: implement adaptive token budget + homogenous bucketing (PR by EOD)
- Marta: add metrics + soft-429 telemetry (dashboard tile)
- Noah: run synthetic KV-heavy workload (short sequences) and post results in this thread
- Samir: include a small unit test to ensure kernel_tagging doesn't affect deterministic outputs
Noah: I'll post the load-test results by morning. Initial sims look promising but we need real canary data.
Lee: FYI: if kernel_tagging required, we'll route tags to scheduler as `preferred_kernel` metadata (no hard pinning).
Marta: noted, will add heatmap to dashboard for kernel selection frequency.
Samir: Thanks. If canary passes at 1h, we flip to gradual rollout 5/25/50/100% over next 2 days, watch p99 and error-rate.
Anya K: Thanks all. :thumbsup: Keep this thread updated with canary numbers and perf-bot reports.
